Q3D extracts conductor matrices of a finite 3D structure: capacitance and
conductance (C/G), and optionally AC resistance and inductance (R/L). Q3D
takes its geometry as **bodies**: each body is an outline with a height range
and a material. There are two ways to get them:

- [Write the bodies yourself](#write-the-bodies-yourself), for simple shapes.
- [Build them from a GeometryPlan snapshot](#build-bodies-from-a-snapshot),
  for components from your PDK. This supports C/G only.

Q3D does not use the GDS mapping from
[AEDT inputs from a GDS file](aedt-inputs.qmd). It uses the same `materials`
mapping from that guide.

## Write the bodies yourself

This example describes the same CPW as the AEDT inputs guide: a signal line,
two ground strips and a substrate.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import (
    MatrixRunControl, Q3dBodySpec, Q3dNetSpec, Q3dSpec, prepare_handoff,
)

bodies = (
    Q3dBodySpec(
        body_id="signal",
        exterior_um=((-250.0, -5.0), (250.0, -5.0),
                     (250.0, 5.0), (-250.0, 5.0)),
        holes_um=(), z_min_um=0.0, z_max_um=0.2,
        material_id="Nb", physical_role="signal", net_id="Signal",
    ),
    Q3dBodySpec(
        body_id="ground_upper",
        exterior_um=((-250.0, 11.0), (250.0, 11.0),
                     (250.0, 91.0), (-250.0, 91.0)),
        holes_um=(), z_min_um=0.0, z_max_um=0.2,
        material_id="Nb", physical_role="ground", net_id="Ground",
    ),
    Q3dBodySpec(
        body_id="ground_lower",
        exterior_um=((-250.0, -91.0), (250.0, -91.0),
                     (250.0, -11.0), (-250.0, -11.0)),
        holes_um=(), z_min_um=0.0, z_max_um=0.2,
        material_id="Nb", physical_role="ground", net_id="Ground",
    ),
    Q3dBodySpec(
        body_id="substrate",
        exterior_um=((-250.0, -91.0), (250.0, -91.0),
                     (250.0, 91.0), (-250.0, 91.0)),
        holes_um=(), z_min_um=-500.0, z_max_um=0.0,
        material_id="Si", physical_role="substrate", net_id=None,
    ),
)
nets = (
    Q3dNetSpec("Signal", "Signal", ("signal",),
               "signal", "-X", "signal", "+X"),
    Q3dNetSpec("Ground", "Ground", ("ground_upper", "ground_lower")),
)
spec = Q3dSpec(
    modeling="solid",
    project_name="cpw_q3d",
    design_name="CpwFiniteGroundQ3d",
    materials=materials, vacuum_material_id="vacuum",
    bodies=bodies, nets=nets,
    run_control=MatrixRunControl("Setup1", frequency_ghz=6.0, maximum_passes=3),
    region_padding_um=(0.0, 0.0, 100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 1000.0),
    solve_ac_rl=True,
)
handoff = prepare_handoff(spec=spec, output_dir=Path(".artifacts/cpw-q3d"))
print(handoff.run_dir)
```

- `Q3dBodySpec` is one body: an outer outline (`exterior_um`), optional holes,
  a height range in micrometres, a material, a role, and the Net it belongs
  to. The substrate belongs to no Net.
- `Q3dNetSpec` groups bodies into a Net. For R/L extraction, a signal Net also
  names a source and a sink face: here the `-X` and `+X` ends of the signal
  body. Every conductor body must be in exactly one Net.
- `MatrixRunControl` sets the extraction frequency in GHz and the maximum
  number of adaptive passes.

The frequency and pass count are example values.

### Choose what to extract

| `solve_ac_rl` | Extracts | Output files in `results/q3d/` |
|---|---|---|
| `True` (default) | C/G and AC R/L | `c_matrix.csv`, `ac_rl_matrix.csv`, `matrices.csv` |
| `False` | C/G only | `c_matrix.csv` |

For C/G only, also drop the source and sink faces from the signal Net.

### Add a grounded enclosure (C/G only)

With `solve_ac_rl=False`, you can surround the model with a grounded box by
setting `grounded_region_net="EnclosureGround"`. The name must differ from
your other Nets. Q3D then places a PEC sheet on each of the six faces of the
region. Your own ground Nets stay separate. See the
[Q3D reference](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q3d-extraction-and-region-ground-candidate).

## Build bodies from a snapshot

For a PDK component, `prepare_q3d_from_geometry` builds the bodies from a
GeometryPlan snapshot. This example uses the snapshot from the
[Xmon model](../tutorial-xmon-input.qmd). It needs the `aedt-epr` extra.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.aedt import MatrixRunControl, prepare_q3d_from_geometry

handoff = prepare_q3d_from_geometry(
    snapshot,
    modeling="solid",
    output_dir=Path(".artifacts/xmon-q3d-cg"),
    project_name="xmon_q3d_cg",
    design_name="XmonQ3dCg",
    materials=materials,
    net_types={"xmon_pad": "Signal", "Ground": "Signal"},
    physical_ground_nets=("Ground",),
    run_control=MatrixRunControl("Setup1", frequency_ghz=6.0, maximum_passes=3),
    region_padding_um=(0.0, 0.0, 100.0, 100.0, 1000.0, 1000.0),
)
print(handoff.run_dir)
```

- `materials` needs one `PdkMaterial` for each material in the snapshot.
- `net_types` sets the Q3D Net type of each Net. Here both Nets are `Signal`,
  so both get rows in the capacitance matrix.
- `physical_ground_nets` marks which Nets are physically ground, separately
  from their Q3D type.

Each body keeps its outline, holes, height range, material and Net from the
snapshot. SCGSim does not guess connectivity. Curved boundaries are not
supported for AEDT; polygons are used.

## Check the model in AEDT without solving

To build the model in AEDT and inspect it without solving, run on the AEDT
computer:

```bash
python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run_dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --execute --prepare-only
```

A run directory used this way cannot be solved afterwards; prepare a new one
for the solve. See [Inspect the prepared run](solver-observations.qmd#aedt-build-the-model-without-solving).

## Run and read the result

[Run the directory](execute.qmd), then [load it](returned-results.qmd). The
matrices keep Q3D's conductor order and units. The adaptive history is
described in [matrix convergence records](../specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q2d-q3d-convergence-observations).

A change of enclosure or of `solve_ac_rl` is a different calculation; prepare
a new run.
